clue.text: Small coin to change? Time to go to town

parts.note: a penny is written 1p, and the figure 1 looks like the letter I

indicators.note: says that the letter for time leaves the word

parts.note: to change is to switch

explanation.surface: Someone wonders about swapping a coin before it is time to head into town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go' takes T out of SWITCH, leaving SWICH. IPSWICH is the county town of Suffolk, in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Ipswich is an English county town, so it is an example of a town.

clue.text: Drunk, I take sweetener without resistance

indicators.note: says the letter for resistance is left out

parts.note: taking a sweetener, a bribe, means saying I'm bribed
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A drinker admits to accepting something sweet without putting up a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetener' looks like sugar but means a bribe; I'M BRIBED loses its R.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbibe is to drink, so having imbibed means having drunk.

clue.text: Indigestion? A most troubled hour in store!

indicators.note: something troubled is disturbed, so these letters are mixed up
puts the letter for hour inside the word for store

parts.note: a cache is a hidden store

explanation.surface: A deeply upsetting hour spent in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' turns A MOST into STOMA; H goes into CACHE to make CHACHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigestion is one cause of a pain in the belly, hence the question mark marking an example.

clue.text: Embellishes pub lounge when talking

indicators.note: says the words are taken by their sound in speech

parts.note: a pub is an inn, and to lounge is to laze

explanation.surface: Someone decorates the comfortable bar of a pub while chatting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lounge' reads as the pub's lounge bar but is the verb laze.
explanation.definitionFit: To inlay is to decorate a surface by setting other material into it, a way of embellishing.

clue.text: Circle essential with each tap dance

parts.note: H and C mark the hot and cold taps
O is round like a circle
key means essential, as in a key point
H and C mark the hot and cold taps
O is round like a circle
key means essential, as in a key point

explanation.surface: Someone says it is vital to tap a circle when dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'each tap' means both taps, H and C, each with O KEY after it. The hokey-cokey is a British party dance, the hokey-pokey in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: The hokey-cokey is a group dance done in a circle, with actions sung out as it goes.

clue.text: Tati said to exploit Zola's work

indicators.note: signals that the film-maker's first name is taken for its sound only

parts.note: Jacques Tati was the French film-maker behind Monsieur Hulot
to exploit is to use

explanation.surface: A French comic film-maker is said to be making use of a novelist's writing.
explanation.walkthrough: JACQUES is said 'zhak', so the sound is written as JACC here.
explanation.definitionFit: Émile Zola's famous 1898 open letter defending Dreyfus bore this title, so it is a named piece of his work.

clue.text: Sacking employee ultimately holding up project

indicators.note: in a down answer the last letter sits below, holding up the rest

parts.note: to project is to jut out

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A worker's eventual dismissal delays the scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sacking' suggests dismissal but is the coarse cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Jute is the coarse plant fibre woven into sacking for bags.

clue.text: Making chemical process where carbon becomes lead

indicators.note: says the named letter moves to the front of the word

parts.note: a reaction is a chemical process
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: An alchemist's experiment in which one element turns into the metal lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like the metal, fitting the chemistry, but means the front position.
explanation.definitionFit: Creation is the act of bringing something into being, a synonym of making.

clue.text: Establishment incomparable, without question European

indicators.note: says the following letters are taken away

parts.note: something incomparable is unique

explanation.surface: A remarkable institution is undoubtedly European.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without question' reads as 'undoubtedly' but takes QU and E from UNIQUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A university is an institution, and uni is its everyday short form.

clue.text: Need AGM arranged close to board meeting

indicators.note: to arrange is to put in a new order, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A company needs an annual general meeting before its directors meet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'board meeting' suggests directors; the board is a chessboard and the meeting a game.
explanation.definitionFit: An endgame is the closing stage of a game of chess, played on a board.

clue.text: A life's work cut short

indicators.note: says the word loses its whole ending, keeping only its opening

parts.note: a written account of someone's life is a biography, one kind of literary work

explanation.surface: Someone's lifetime of effort is ended early.
explanation.walkthrough: BIO is the common short form of biography.
explanation.definitionFit: A bio is a short written account of a person's career and history, informally called a life.

clue.text: Fleet with keel in splinters departs

indicators.note: something in splinters is smashed into bits, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: A ship whose keel breaks into pieces leaves port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'splinters' shuffles WITH KEEL IN into LIKETHEWIN, then D goes on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To move like the wind is to go very fast, and fleet is an adjective meaning swift.

clue.text: Repeat you drop leading viewer to be suspicious?

indicators.note: puts the word for drop at the front of the rest

parts.note: a bead is a small drop of liquid, as in a bead of sweat

indicators.note: says the old word for you is written twice in a row

parts.note: ye is an old form of you

explanation.surface: Someone told to say it again drops a lead in the hope of looking dubious.
explanation.walkthrough: BEAD comes first and YE is written twice: BEAD + YE + YE.
explanation.definitionFit: A beady eye is a watchful, distrustful gaze, so it is a viewer kept on something suspect.

clue.text: More work leads to unusual type of pain in arm

indicators.note: the leading letters of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: Extra exertion brings on a strange kind of ache in the arm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More' is not the comparative but Sir Thomas More, author of the 1516 book Utopia.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Thomas More wrote Utopia, so it is literally a work by More.

clue.text: Helsinki couple, one only speaking English as penned in Trollope novel

indicators.note: only the first of the pair is taken by sound, so its spelling changes

parts.note: two people from Helsinki are two Finns
two people from Helsinki are two Finns

explanation.surface: Two people from Helsinki, only one of them talking English, are written into a Victorian novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one only speaking' means just the first Finn is spelt by its sound. Anthony Trollope wrote the novel in 1869.
explanation.definitionFit: Phineas Finn is one of Anthony Trollope's Palliser novels, named after its Irish hero.

clue.text: Use shower for cleaning, washing etc.

definitions.text: Use shower for cleaning, washing etc.

parts.words: Use shower for cleaning, washing etc
parts.note: reads as advice to take a shower, but describes a device that shows how much household supply is used for cleaning and washing

explanation.surface: Advice to take a shower to get clean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shower' is not a spray of water but a thing that shows, here showing use.
explanation.definitionFit: A water meter records how much a household consumes for washing and the like.

clue.text: Scuttle back to a Gulf resort

indicators.note: says the word for the coal container is read backwards

parts.note: a hod is a coal scuttle, a bucket for carrying coal

explanation.surface: Someone hurries back to a holiday spot by the Persian Gulf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scuttle' looks like a verb meaning hurry; here it is the coal bucket.
explanation.definitionFit: Doha, capital of Qatar, is a city on the Persian Gulf visited by holidaymakers.

clue.text: Sheepish following attempted kick at climber

indicators.note: puts the word for sheepish after the pieces before it

parts.note: a pot is a shot at goal, an attempt at something
ovine means of or like sheep

explanation.surface: A timid player follows up a failed shot at goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheepish' suggests embarrassed, but here it means literally like a sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: The potato plant's trailing stem is a vine, and a vine is a climbing plant.

clue.text: Invading pitch is, they say, dying out

indicators.note: says one piece enters the other

parts.note: to pitch is to throw, as is to fling

indicators.note: says the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like IZZ

explanation.surface: An encroachment onto the field is said to be fading away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'they say' asks for the sound of 'is', which rhymes with fizz; 'pitch' looks like a sports field but is the verb throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fizzling out is gradually ending, so it is dying out.

clue.text: Old scientist agreed to cut a holiday short

indicators.note: says one word is cut into, with the other set inside it
says the word for holiday loses its last letter

parts.note: a rest is a break or holiday
to chime is to agree, as in views that chime

explanation.surface: An elderly scientist consented to curtail a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims REST to RES; A + RES is cut open by CHIMED to give AR-CHIMED-ES.
explanation.definitionFit: Archimedes was an ancient Greek mathematician and inventor, so he is a scientist from long ago.

clue.text: Did Don like me visiting South of France?

parts.note: as means like

indicators.note: says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: sud is the French word for south

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether Don enjoyed my trip to the south of France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' looks like a man's name but is the verb to put on.
explanation.definitionFit: To don clothes is to put them on, and assumed is the past tense of assume, which also means put on.

clue.text: Second letter to the Corinthians

parts.note: reads like the Bible's Second Epistle to the Corinthians, but means the second character of the alphabet used by the Greeks of Corinth

explanation.surface: A book of the New Testament addressed by St Paul to the church in Corinth.
explanation.definitionFit: Beta is the second character of the Greek alphabet, the script the Corinthians read.

clue.text: Injured before and after a walk in Spain

parts.note: taken as written, once before and once after
lamed means injured so as to limp

explanation.surface: A hiker hurt before and after a stroll in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before and after a' puts an A on both sides of LAMED.
explanation.definitionFit: An alameda is a tree-lined public promenade in Spain, a place for walking.

clue.text: Mountain a painter captured in drawing

indicators.note: says the first pieces are held inside the word for drawing

parts.note: drawing is a form of art
RA stands for Royal Academician, a painter

explanation.surface: A peak that an artist caught in a sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captured in' places the pair between the second and third letters. Ararat stands in eastern Turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: Ararat is the mountain in Turkey where Noah's ark is said to have come to rest.

clue.text: Happy colleague frequently in fits?

parts.note: Happy is one of the seven dwarfs, and his workmate prone to fits is the one who keeps sneezing

explanation.surface: A cheerful co-worker who keeps having seizures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Happy' is not an adjective but the name of one of Snow White's seven dwarfs.
explanation.definitionFit: Sneezy is another of the seven dwarfs, named for his bouts of sneezing.

clue.text: A 26 9's awfully good food

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done badly, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the answer to 26 down is used here
the answer to 9 across with the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: A clue built from two other answers claims the result is very tasty fare.
explanation.walkthrough: The numbers point to the answers at 26 down and 9 across; 'awfully' shuffles them with the possessive's S.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambrosia was the food of the Greek gods, and the word now means any delicious food.

clue.text: Oath sworn as attorney rises

indicators.note: in a down answer, rising means read from bottom to top

parts.note: DA is a district attorney in the US

explanation.surface: A promise made when a lawyer stands up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sworn' links the definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Egad is a mild old-fashioned exclamation, a minced oath.

clue.text: Early Times pitch for smaller rival?

definitions.text: Early Times pitch for smaller rival?

parts.words: Early Times pitch for smaller rival
parts.note: reads as a sales pitch by a rival paper, but points to the planet seen before dawn, which is also the title of a small British left-wing daily

explanation.surface: A competing smaller newspaper makes a play for readers of The Times in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: The Morning Star is a small left-wing British daily paper; the morning star is also Venus seen before sunrise.
explanation.definitionFit: Venus seen before dawn is called the morning star, and a newspaper of that name competes with The Times.

clue.text: Object to batter with what comes after fish

definitions.meaning: a battering device used to knock down gates
in the zodiac, Pisces the fish is followed by Aries

explanation.surface: Someone objects to using fish batter.

explanation.definitionFit: A ram is a battering engine, and the ram is the symbol of Aries, the sign after Pisces.

clue.text: Take on Hearts away in heat

parts.note: to take on a worker is to hire them

explanation.surface: A card player sheds the hearts in a heated moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Heat can mean anger or passion, as in the heat of the moment, which is what ire is.

clue.text: Hero returning like St Paul's "welcoming soldier"

explanation.walkthrough: The reversal makes DOGIMED read backwards; 'St Paul's' is the domed London cathedral.
